purpose: Standard interpretation/reporting layer for 1W/4W/12W forward OOS checkpoints. Validation-only; never changes model logic.

report_sections.title: Dove ha funzionato il modello
report_sections.interpretation_rule: Do not generalize from tiny buckets; always report n alongside hit rate.

report_sections.title: Pair principali
report_sections.interpretation_rule: Pairs without a canonical favored side remain excluded from hit-rate scoring.

report_sections.title: Diagnostica del segnale
report_sections.interpretation_rule: Descriptive only. No threshold or hierarchy change inside the active OOS window.

report_sections.title: Cosa ci sta dicendo il checkpoint

1W.allowed_conclusion: Check execution, directionality and obvious failures; never tune from 1W alone.

4W.allowed_conclusion: Assess persistence by quality bucket and whether structural contrasts outperform partial advantages; still no tuning unless a hard implementation defect is proven.

12W.allowed_conclusion: Combine 1W/4W/12W and decide whether evidence justifies post-OOS research on thresholds, turning persistence, confidence modifiers or pair hierarchy.

hard_guardrails: No use of post-checkpoint data beyond the first common ECB fixing on/after the evaluation date.
No rewriting T0 states or anchors after observing outcomes.
No model weights, thresholds, hierarchy, pair logic, or runtime changes during the active OOS regime.
Any genuine model-rule change restarts out-of-sample from a new T0.
Always report sample size together with hit rate.
Separate implementation/data defects from model-performance misses.
final_cycle_questions: Do CONTRASTO STRUTTURALE FORTE pairs outperform VANTAGGIO RELATIVO PARZIALE?
Does performance improve from 1W to 4W/12W as historical pseudo-OOS suggested?
Are misses concentrated in price-divergent signals or in one macro/policy configuration?
Does the model add useful discrimination versus no-favored-side pairs without forcing a winner?
Is there enough independent evidence to justify a new rule research cycle?
